clinical_inconsistencies.issue: Patients labelled 'notckd' but assigned an advanced CKD stage (s3-s5)
clinical_inconsistencies.interpretation: Either the outcome label or the stage assignment is wrong for these records. Reported, not corrected: we have no external source of truth to arbitrate.

clinical_inconsistencies.issue: Patients labelled 'notckd' whose eGFR band is below 60 mL/min/1.73m2
clinical_inconsistencies.interpretation: An eGFR below 60 sustained over three months is itself a CKD-defining criterion, so these labels are internally inconsistent with the eGFR column. Chronicity cannot be verified from a single cross-sectional record, which is one possible benign explanation.

grf_p_investigation.conclusion: A single cell in 'grf' contains the token ' p ' (letter p with surrounding whitespace), which is not an interval label. The affected patient is labelled ckd and staged s5; every other s5 patient in the file falls in the lowest eGFR band. The most parsimonious reading is a data-entry error in the eGFR field. Because the true value cannot be recovered, the cell is treated as MISSING and imputed inside training folds only. The raw file is preserved unmodified at data/raw/. Note that 'grf' is excluded from every clinically valid configuration, so this defect can only affect the deliberately invalid leaky_model.

variable_inventory.name: age
variable_inventory.description: Patient age, released as 10 ordered bins from '< 12' to '>= 74' (years).
variable_inventory.rationale: Age is recorded at registration at no marginal cost and is a well-established CKD risk factor.

variable_inventory.name: bp (Diastolic)
variable_inventory.description: Diastolic blood pressure indicator, released as a binary 0/1 flag.
variable_inventory.rationale: Blood pressure is measured with a reusable sphygmomanometer; the marginal cost per patient is effectively zero.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: The column is named for diastolic pressure but ships as a binary 0/1 flag, so the underlying mmHg value and the threshold that produced the flag are both unrecoverable. The direction of the coding (1 = elevated) is inferred from its association with 'bp limit' and 'htn', not from documentation.

variable_inventory.name: bp limit
variable_inventory.description: Three-level blood-pressure indicator (0/1/2).
variable_inventory.rationale: Derived from the same sphygmomanometer reading as 'bp (Diastolic)', so it adds no marginal cost.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Undocumented. Empirically it refines 'bp (Diastolic)': every patient with bp (Diastolic)=0 has bp limit=0, while bp (Diastolic)=1 splits across all three levels. It is therefore most likely a graded severity band, but the mmHg cut-points are unknown and are NOT reconstructed here.

variable_inventory.name: htn
variable_inventory.description: Hypertension, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Elicited as history or read from an existing chart entry; no consumables required.

variable_inventory.name: dm
variable_inventory.description: Diabetes mellitus, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Treated as a history item: a previously established diagnosis is free to elicit at screening. Verified empirically NOT to be a deterministic function of the blood-glucose column, so it carries independent history information.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: A first-time diabetes diagnosis requires a glucose assay, so in a population with poor prior healthcare contact this variable would be less freely available than assumed here.

variable_inventory.name: cad
variable_inventory.description: Coronary artery disease, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Recorded as a prior diagnosis during history taking; free to elicit at the point of screening.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Establishing CAD de novo is expensive. Its value as a *screening* predictor depends on patients already knowing the diagnosis.

variable_inventory.name: appet
variable_inventory.description: Appetite, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: A single symptom question; no cost.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Polarity (whether 1 denotes poor or good appetite) is not documented in the released file.

variable_inventory.name: pe
variable_inventory.description: Pedal oedema, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Established by inspection and palpation of the ankles; no consumables.

variable_inventory.name: ane
variable_inventory.description: Anaemia, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Conservatively tiered as laboratory-derived. Anaemia is defined by a haemoglobin concentration, and in a dataset that also ships 'hemo' the most likely provenance of this flag is the full blood count.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: IMPORTANT AND CONSEQUENTIAL. Anaemia can also be recorded clinically (conjunctival or palmar pallor) at no cost. We verified that 'ane' is NOT a deterministic function of the 'hemo' bins (for example 25 patients with hemo 10-11.3 are ane=0 while 3 are ane=1), so it is not a pure re-coding of haemoglobin. Because provenance cannot be established from the file, it is EXCLUDED from the low-cost configuration. This is the conservative choice: it can only understate low-cost performance, never inflate it.

variable_inventory.name: sg
variable_inventory.description: Urine specific gravity, 5 ordered bins from '< 1.007' to '>= 1.023'.
variable_inventory.rationale: Read directly from a urine reagent strip; non-invasive and among the cheapest measurements available in any clinic.

variable_inventory.name: al
variable_inventory.description: Urine albumin, 5 ordered bins ('< 0' to '>= 4'), i.e. a dipstick protein/albumin grade.
variable_inventory.rationale: Read from the same urine reagent strip as 'sg'; non-invasive and cheap. Albuminuria is one of the two axes on which CKD is defined, which makes it both the most clinically relevant and the most scrutinised low-cost variable in this study.

variable_inventory.name: su
variable_inventory.description: Urine sugar, 6 bins from '< 0' to '>= 4'.
variable_inventory.rationale: Read from the same urine reagent strip; non-invasive and cheap.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: The published bin edges for this column are internally inconsistent and overlapping ('1 - 2' vs '2 - 2'; '3 - 4' vs '4 - 4' vs '>= 4'), so its ordinal encoding contains ties. Reported as a data-quality defect; not silently repaired.

variable_inventory.name: rbc
variable_inventory.description: Red blood cells in urine, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Requires urine microscopy: non-invasive to the patient, but needs a microscope and a trained operator, so it is not free at the point of community screening.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Could in principle refer to a blood-count red-cell abnormality rather than urinary red cells, but its position among the urinalysis columns and the presence of a separate 'rbcc' (red blood cell count) column make urinary microscopy the far more likely reading.

variable_inventory.name: pc
variable_inventory.description: Pus cells in urine, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

variable_inventory.name: pcc
variable_inventory.description: Pus cell clumps in urine, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

variable_inventory.name: ba
variable_inventory.description: Bacteria in urine, binary 0/1.
variable_inventory.rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

variable_inventory.name: bgr
variable_inventory.description: Blood glucose (random), 10 bins from '< 112' to '>= 448' mg/dL.
variable_inventory.rationale: Venous or capillary blood assay.

variable_inventory.name: bu
variable_inventory.description: Blood urea, 8 bins from '< 48.1' to '>= 352.9' mg/dL.
variable_inventory.rationale: Serum chemistry panel; requires venepuncture and an analyser.

variable_inventory.name: sc
variable_inventory.description: Serum creatinine, 7 bins from '< 3.65' to '>= 28.85' mg/dL.
variable_inventory.rationale: Serum chemistry panel; requires venepuncture and an analyser.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Serum creatinine is the input to the eGFR equation that defines 'grf' and 'stage'. It is retained in the valid laboratory configuration because it is a genuine, routinely measured screening analyte rather than a diagnostic label, but it is the variable most likely to behave as a near-proxy for the outcome, and results are interpreted with that in mind.

variable_inventory.name: sod
variable_inventory.description: Serum sodium, 9 bins from '< 118' to '>= 158' mEq/L.
variable_inventory.rationale: Serum electrolyte panel; requires venepuncture.

variable_inventory.name: pot
variable_inventory.description: Serum potassium, 4 bins from '< 7.31' to '>= 42.59' mEq/L.
variable_inventory.rationale: Serum electrolyte panel; requires venepuncture.
variable_inventory.uncertainty_note: Near-constant: 197 of 200 patients fall in the single bin '< 7.31'. The upper bins ('38.18 - 42.59', '>= 42.59') lie far outside any survivable serum potassium range and are almost certainly recording errors. Flagged, retained as-is, and carries essentially no usable information.

variable_inventory.name: hemo
variable_inventory.description: Haemoglobin, 10 bins from '< 6.1' to '>= 16.5' g/dL.
variable_inventory.rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture and an analyser.

variable_inventory.name: pcv
variable_inventory.description: Packed cell volume (haematocrit), 10 bins from '< 17.9' to '>= 49.1' percent.
variable_inventory.rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

variable_inventory.name: rbcc
variable_inventory.description: Red blood cell count, 9 bins from '< 2.69' to '>= 7.41' (millions/uL).
variable_inventory.rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

variable_inventory.name: wbcc
variable_inventory.description: White blood cell count, 9 bins from '< 4980' to '>= 24020' (cells/uL).
variable_inventory.rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

variable_inventory.name: grf
variable_inventory.description: Glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), 10 bins plus one invalid entry.
variable_inventory.rationale: eGFR is computed from serum creatinine and is the quantity that *defines* CKD stage. Using it to predict CKD is close to using the diagnostic criterion itself as a predictor.

variable_inventory.name: stage
variable_inventory.description: CKD stage s1 to s5.
variable_inventory.rationale: A staging label assigned after diagnosis. Empirically it is a deterministic banding of 'grf' in this file, and stages s3 and s5 are 100 percent CKD, so it encodes the outcome almost directly.

variable_inventory.name: affected
variable_inventory.description: Binary 0/1 flag.
variable_inventory.rationale: An exact one-to-one copy of the outcome 'class' in all 200 rows (ckd maps to 1, notckd maps to 0). It is the target, renamed.

variable_inventory.name: class
variable_inventory.description: Outcome: 'ckd' or 'notckd'.
variable_inventory.rationale: The prediction target.

encoding.strategy: Stateless per-cell mapping of each interval label to a representative numeric value (midpoint for closed bins, the finite edge for open-ended bins). Uses no cross-row statistics and therefore cannot leak between folds.
